theorems.name: northBeforeEast_mono
theorems.description: northBeforeEast is monotone: North steps accumulated before a later East step is at least as many as before an earlier East step.

theorems.name: northBeforeEast_le_northSteps
theorems.description: northBeforeEast l k counts a prefix of North steps, bounded by total northSteps.

theorems.name: colEntry_le_northSteps
theorems.description: At column m, the entry y-offset is bounded by total North steps.

theorems.name: nonIntersecting_entry_order
theorems.description: KEY LEMMA: Non-intersecting + P₁ enters column k below P₂ implies P₁ enters column k+1 below P₂. Proof: if P₁ exits above P₂'s entry, a shared y-value exists in both column ranges.

theorems.name: crossing_lemma
theorems.description: THE 2D CROSSING LEMMA: If y₁ < y₂ (P₁ starts lower) but y₂+n₂ < y₁+n₁ (P₁ ends higher), the paths cannot be non-intersecting. Proved by induction on columns using nonIntersecting_entry_order.

theorems.name: path_count_eq_choose
theorems.description: PROVED: The number of lattice paths with m East and n North steps equals C(m+n, m). Proved by induction using pathSplitEquiv bijection and Pascal's identity.

theorems.name: lgv_lemma_2x2
theorems.description: OPEN (sorry): The 2×2 LGV Lemma. NI pair count = lgvDet. Proof strategy: Lindström involution swaps tails of intersecting pairs at first meeting column, creating a bijection with crossing pairs. Crossing Lemma ensures all crossing pairs are intersecting.

theorems.name: vandermonde
theorems.description: PROVED: Vandermonde's Identity C(m+n, r) = Σ C(m,k)*C(n,r-k) via Mathlib's add_choose_eq.

theorems.name: catalan_formula
theorems.description: PROVED: Catalan formula Cn(n)*(n+1) = C(2n,n) via absorption identity argument.

theorems.name: ballot_formula
theorems.description: PROVED: ballotSeqCount p q * (p+q) = (p-q) * C(p+q,p) for q < p. Proved via absorption identity and Pascal's rule.

theorems.name: ballot_via_path_count
theorems.description: PROVED: ballot count = |pathType q (p-1)| - |pathType (q-1) p|. This is the 1D reflection principle: bad ballot sequences biject with shifted paths.

theorems.name: splitAfterEast_append
theorems.description: PROVED: Splitting a path and rejoining gives back the original path.
